 THIS CRL.P. IS FILED U/S.482 OF CR.P.C., PRAYING TO QUASH THE ENTIRE PROCEEDINGS OF THE CR.NO.54/2023 REGISTERED BY THE AREHALLI POLICE FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 504, 323, 354 AND 506 OF IPC, NOW PENDING ON THE FILE OF CIVIL JUDGE (JR.DN.) AND J.M.F.C., BELURU IN C.C.NO.651/2023.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA
ORAL ORDER

The petitioner is before this Court calling in question the registration of a crime in Crime No.54/2023 registered for offences punishable under Sections 504, 323, 354 and 506 and the proceedings in C.C.No.651/2023.
2.
Heard Sri. G.J. Chandra, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Sri.

Thejesh P., learned HCGP appearing for respondent No.1.
NC: 2024:KHC:37106 3.

Facts in brief, germane, are as follows:
The petitioner and respondent No.2 are said to have had a loan transaction.

On 03.07.2023, a crime comes to be registered in Crime No.54/2023 alleging that six days prior to the registration of the crime, the petitioner had threatened the complainant when she had asked the return of the loan, not only threatened, but also had outraged the modesty of the complainant.
Therefore, the complaint comes to be registered.
The police after investigation file a charge sheet.
Filing of the charge sheet is what has driven the petitioner to this Court in the subject petition.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the first complaint was sought to be registered on 06.07.2023, which is rendered a non-cognizable report.
Thereafter, the complainant improves the version and registers the impugned complaint for adding offences punishable under Section 376 of the IPC as well.
Therefore, he would submit that the improvement in the complaint would enure to the benefit of the petitioner towards quashment of the proceedings.

Learned HCGP would however refute the submissions to contend that this fact is also taken note of while filing the charge sheet and the offence is clearly made out while filing the charge sheet by the jurisdictional police.
6. I have given my anxious consideration to the respective submissions made by the learned counsel and have perused the material on record.
7. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.
The afore-narrated facts are matter of record qua the transaction between the petitioner and the complainant.
